source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Press load default,save and reboot.
3. Boot in BIOS,compare setting should matches SPEC.
4. Change BIOS all/random setting in this function,to non-default  setting.
5. Save and reboot.
6. Boot in BIOS and check your setting still exist.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The default setting should matches SPEC."
2. No error log happen.
3. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
4. Check your set still exist.

original_test_intent: Verify the platform's UEFI Driver Health page defaults and persistence for any documented configurable controls while preserving accurate driver/controller health, critical-device availability and required repair/reconnect/reboot behavior.
original_method: Manually load defaults, inspect named Driver Health entries and any documented controls, apply only bounded supported changes/actions, save/reboot, verify persistence or action result and correlate UEFI driver/controller handles with OS devices and boot health.
manual_activity: An engineer must inspect the UEFI Driver Health page, distinguish status from configuration/repair actions, perform only approved UI operations and visually verify results. OS driver health is supporting evidence only.
required_inputs: Exact page entries, health/status meanings, configurable fields and repair/configure/reconnect/reboot semantics
Mapping from driver/controller/child handles to persistent storage, network, console and other device identities
SPEC defaults and approved bounded actions/values
Approved final state and expected status freshness
safety_requirements: Do not operationalize all/random or treat every health entry as a persistent setting; some entries may be status or one-shot repair actions.
Do not invoke repair, configuration, reconnect, disconnect or firmware-driver actions without device-specific approval.
Protect boot storage, management NIC, console/display and recovery devices; capture persistent identities before any action.
Do not clear or mask an unhealthy state merely to obtain a healthy display; preserve original failure evidence.
Stop on critical-device loss, new unhealthy status, boot failure, unexpected driver binding or management loss.
Restore the approved final state; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only UEFI driver/boot information where exposed, PCI/storage/network/device persistent identities, OS driver bindings/health, logs and BMC status.
Correlate exact page entries and timestamps with downstream device evidence around operator phases.
Do not drive BIOS, invoke repair/configuration, bind/unbind drivers or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve page-entry semantics, supported actions/values, critical-device map and recovery.
Perform and capture default-first inspection and any bounded configuration/action sequence.
Determine whether page status and downstream evidence satisfy acceptance and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects remote BIOS execution. No source command exists; OS driver reload/bind operations are not equivalent to UEFI Driver Health protocol behavior.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the firmware page method and add version-recorded, read-only UEFI/OS driver, device and boot evidence without invoking repair or rebinding.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source default-first lifecycle, null script and 5/20-minute fields are retained; all/random is not operationalized and action-versus-persistence semantics must be documented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Inventory each displayed UEFI driver/controller/child entry, classify it as status, configurable setting or action, map it to persistent devices, and define the expected state transition and reset requirement before execution.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact UEFI implementation and installed drivers/controllers on the selected BIOS build.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC, UEFI driver/device firmware, OS/kernel/driver and inventory-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform Driver Health page documentation and applicable UEFI driver/vendor guidance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces random changes with entry-specific state/action semantics and critical-device mapping.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; preserves default/persistence where applicable and adds status freshness, action result and device continuity coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Page schema, entry/handle map, expected transitions, reset and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS driver state cannot prove UEFI health-protocol status and some health entries may be transient or action-only.

project_override_considerations: A project may scope named drivers/controllers and supported actions. Results must distinguish status, configuration and action entries and list excluded devices; they cannot claim all driver health.
expected_evidence: Platform/driver identity, page-entry semantics, critical-device map, approval and recovery
Baseline Driver Health captures plus UEFI/OS driver, device and boot evidence
Load Default captures and SPEC comparison for truly persistent fields
Approved action/change captures, expected transition, reset and downstream device results
Approved final state, preserved anomalies and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The generic procedure is imprecise for a mixed status/action page, but the item does not prove that no configurable fields exist. Entry semantics are readiness inputs; no explicit contradictory result is stated.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The page-level intent is understandable. Exact entries and actions must be defined before execution, but that project/platform detail does not permanently block the master case.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees on manual firmware operation and adds protocol-entry/action and critical-device safeguards.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its UEFI/OS driver evidence while correcting classification to MANUAL ONLY and distinguishing health from actions.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Prevents OS driver operations from substituting for UEFI acceptance and preserves original unhealthy evidence.

review_improvement: Avoids treating health indicators or one-shot repair actions as ordinary persistent settings and ties every page entry to the affected physical function.
independent_technical_reasoning: The core evidence is the firmware Driver Health UI and any operator-invoked UEFI action. Automated inventories only corroborate device consequences, so MANUAL ONLY is required.
no_automatic_retry: Do not automatically repeat Driver Health actions, configuration changes, reconnects or reboots after status or device anomalies; preserve first evidence and obtain engineer disposition.
